nav.limits: What it does and does not do
home.title: Vessel
home.lead: A VPN run by the anoni.net community. The connection is disguised so it is harder to recognize as a VPN, which helps on networks that block VPNs. You sign up without an email address or phone number, and the keys for your connection are made in your own browser, where the community's servers cannot reach them.
home.inviteOnly: Invites come from community members only, and places are limited.
how.title: How it works
how.1.title: Redeem an invite
how.1.body: Enter your invite code and you get a 16-digit account number. You sign in with it from then on.
how.2.title: Add a device
how.2.body: Pick the city of the node, name the device, and choose whether to block malicious sites and ads. Keys are generated in your browser, and the private key never reaches the community's servers.
how.3.title: Import into the app
how.3.body: Scan the QR code with the AmneziaWG app or import the downloaded file, then switch it on.
limits.title: What it does and does not do
limits.can.1: Your network provider sees only that you connect to a Vessel node, not where you go from there
limits.can.2: The connection is obfuscated, so it is less likely to be recognized and blocked as a VPN
limits.can.3: Reach sites that are blocked on your network
limits.can.4: Block malicious sites or ads if you choose, filtered by the node's DNS resolver, which keeps no query logs
limits.cannot.1: Make you anonymous: the community's nodes can see which domains you connect to. Use Tor Browser when you need anonymity
limits.cannot.2: Hide your accounts: once you sign in to Google or Facebook, they still know it is you
limits.cannot.3: Guarantee it works on every network, since blocking keeps changing
data.title: What we keep
data.kept.1: A hash of your account number, which cannot be turned back into the number
data.kept.2: When the account was created and last signed in to
data.kept.3: Each device's name, public key, city and expiry date
data.notKept.1: Email, phone number or any other contact details
data.notKept.3: Where you connect to, or when
data.cloudflare: This site goes through Cloudflare, which can see visitors' IP addresses and the pages they view.
data.stats: Views of public pages go to the community's self-hosted Umami, which works out the country and city from the IP address but does not keep the address. Pages after sign-in are not recorded, and nothing about accounts or devices is sent.
data.details: Details are in the privacy policy

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.invite.q: How do I get an invite code?
faq.invite.a: During the test, codes go out through the anoni.net newsletter, one per subscriber. Places are limited, and whether more go out depends on how the first round is used.
faq.cost.a: No. Community volunteers run it. Plans for after the test will be announced separately.
faq.lost.q: What if I lose my account number?
faq.lost.a: It cannot be recovered. The community has no email address for you and keeps only a hash of the number, so you would need a new invite code. A password manager is a good place to keep it.
faq.number.q: The account number is only digits. Is that safe?
faq.number.a: Sixteen digits give ten quadrillion combinations, and sign-in attempts are rate limited, so guessing is not practical. The database stores only a keyed hash of the number, which is hard to reverse even if the database leaks.
faq.share.q: Can my family use my account?
faq.share.a: An account holds up to 3 devices sharing 50 GB a month, so family devices are fine. Anyone with the account number can also see and delete your devices, so share it only with people you trust. Accounts and invite codes must not be sold.
faq.app.q: Why can't I use the regular WireGuard® app?
faq.app.a: Vessel disguises its connections with AmneziaWG, so its packets look different from regular WireGuard, and the regular app cannot use the config.
faq.ios.q: AmneziaWG is missing from my App Store
faq.ios.a: It is not listed in some regions. iPhones have no other way to install it, so the only option is an Apple ID from another region. On Android you can install the APK instead.
faq.twoDevices.q: Can I use one config on two devices?
faq.twoDevices.a: No. Two devices connected at once keep taking the connection from each other and drop out often. Create a config for each device, up to 3 per account.
faq.newPhone.q: What about a new phone or a reinstall?
faq.newPhone.a: A config is shown only once, when it is created, and the community's servers do not have the private key. Delete the old device from your list and create a new one.
faq.filter.q: Which domain filter should I pick?
faq.filter.a: Blocking malicious sites uses HaGeZi's Threat Intelligence Feeds (mini), and blocking ads adds HaGeZi Multi (Normal). The lists are updated daily. If unsure, pick no filtering. The ad list sometimes blocks sites that work fine. To change it later, delete the device and create it again. Browsers with “secure DNS” turned on skip the filter.
faq.trouble.a: Make sure AmneziaWG is up to date, then try another network, such as mobile data instead of Wi-Fi. If it still fails, delete the device and create it again. The disguise makes blocking less likely, but no network is guaranteed to work.
faq.speed.a: It depends on your network and how far you are from the node. In the community's tests from Taiwan to the Singapore node, latency was about 67 ms and speed about 200 Mbps.
faq.cities.q: Will there be nodes in other cities?
faq.cities.a: Singapore is the only one for now. More will follow depending on how the test goes.
faq.expire.a: If an account does not sign in to the portal for 30 days, its devices expire and go offline, so unused configs do not linger on the nodes. Each sign-in extends them by 30 days.
faq.quota.a: The account's devices pause and resume automatically at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of the month. Nothing needs to be set up again.
faq.p2p.a: The terms ban BitTorrent and other P2P file sharing during the test. Nodes also block outgoing TCP port 25, so you cannot send mail straight to a mail server on port 25. Port 587, which mail apps normally use, is not affected.
faq.see.q: Can the community see what I do?
faq.see.a: Nodes handle the domains and IP addresses you connect to, but not the contents of HTTPS connections. Nodes keep no logs of them, and the DNS resolvers do not log queries. Using a VPN moves the trust you place in your network provider to the community. Use Tor Browser when you need anonymity.
faq.law.q: What would the community hand over to law enforcement?
faq.law.a: Only what is listed under “What we keep”. There are no connection logs, so an exit IP address and a time cannot be traced to an account.
faq.cloudflare.q: Why does the portal go through Cloudflare?
faq.cloudflare.a: To stop attack traffic. Cloudflare can see visitors' IP addresses and the pages they view. VPN connections do not go through Cloudflare.
faq.delete.q: How do I delete my account?
faq.delete.a: Delete it on the account page. All devices disconnect right away and the data is deleted with them. Database backups disappear after their retention period, which the privacy policy states.
stats.note: Views of public pages go to the community's self-hosted Umami. Pages after sign-in are not recorded.
stats.stopped: Recording is off in this browser.
stats.declined: Your browser asks not to be tracked, so nothing is recorded.
